newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Three dead, 187 injured in Ecuador barracks blast.
newsitem.headline: Three dead, 187 injured in Ecuador barracks blast.

text.p: At least three people were killed and 187 injured when an explosion tore through an Ecuadoran Army ammunition store on a military base near the capital Quito on Tuesday, officials said.
"We have received about 190 cases, three of whom were dead. We think one officer and two soldiers were among the victims," said Edgar Caicedo, director of a military hospital.
Most of the injured were suffering from light wounds although eight underwent surgery and two were in a serious condition, Caicedo said. Three firemen were among the wounded.
Army officials blamed the blast on a fire in an ammunitions storage area in the Las Balvinas military complex, about 12 miles (20 km) outside Quito.
"Unfortunately the fire could not be controlled and it spread to the rest of the sector," Defence Minister Ramiro Ricaurte said.

Army units were sifting through the area of the explosion which caused damage in a radius more than a mile (2 km) wide. About 20 buildings were affected by the blast as well as some helicopters which were slightly damaged.
"We can't get to the area because a clean-up is underway and explosives are being taken away by teams. We are evaluating the damage," said General Jorge Salinas, the army's chief of staff.
Other military officials ruled out the possibility that the explosion had been caused deliberately.

"A commission is investigating the cause of the accident. I reject the possibility of sabotage because maintenance personnel were working at the time in the dump," said General Cesar Duran, the head of Ecuador's army.
An eyewitness told local Radio Quito: "It was a tremendous explosion. Then I saw the bodies lying on the ground. There are civilians' homes near the site of the explosion."
